answer: In an agent economy, resistance to fake identities emerges when each participant must sustain a terrace of graded original contributions over successive epochs. An attacker aiming to flood the network must light an ember of genuine reasoning for every identity, because peer juries reject templates and near-duplicates. The vertex of the defense is that the scarce resource is high-quality judgment itself: spawning thousands of identities multiplies the attacker's real compute bill while diluting any single fake's standing, making mass Sybil creation economically unattractive.
